title: Start an asynchronous computation on the caller
goal: Start a blocking async prefix on the caller, outside a SynchronizationContext.

selectionNotes: Blocking; reject an ambient SynchronizationContext. RC2 can post continuations to it.

prerequisites: Use an F# net11.0 executable or library, .NET 11 SDK, FSharp.Core 11 and LangVersion=11.0.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Use the .NET 11 SDK and its F# compiler for the declared target.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This verified edition targets net11.0; the .NET 10 sample is a comparison, not an older-target catalogue route.

language.name: F#
language.reason: Compiled in stable F# 11 language mode.

constraints: Blocks the caller for the whole operation; never use it to make a UI responsive. Context-affine continuations can deadlock a blocked thread.

Actual pinned RC2 execution posts to a supplied recording context after suspension. The context probe and guard address this source/artifact mismatch; they do not establish safety for every UI framework.
Only the prefix before suspension is guaranteed to start on the caller. Later execution can move threads.

packages.name: FSharp.Core
packages.reason: FSharp.Core 11 is the library dependency for this edition; the exact compiled RC2 version is recorded separately in evidence.

evidence.scope: Actual FSharpAsync compilation and managed execution including start assertions; separate compiler/external-consumer probes in eng/Test-FSharpBoundaries.ps1. No mocks, cross-compilation, native/AOT deployment or GA execution claimed.
